title: lsCOMP: Efficient Light Source Compression
problem: Light source facilities generate X-ray data at 250 GB/s currently, projected to exceed 1 TB/s by end of decade. Intense data streams create critical I/O and bandwidth bottlenecks for data offload to HPC systems. Local processing capacity insufficient for online analysis.
motivation: Synchrotron and free-electron laser facilities produce world-class scientific data but are limited by data management capability. Compression at source reduces bandwidth requirements for data transfer and storage. Current GPU compression tools insufficient for sustained TB/s-level rates with quality preservation.
method: lsCOMP runs a single processing kernel on a GPU to compress X-ray data from light sources, supporting both lossless compression (keeping all original data) and lossy compression with adjustable precision (trading quality for smaller file size). It achieves 380-509 gigabytes per second throughput in lossless mode and can randomly access compressed data at terabyte-per-second speeds, making it practical for near-real-time data handling. The system works with multiple types of light source data formats.
key_novelty: A GPU compressor built for light source data that can sustain 250+ gigabytes per second processing rates today and 1+ terabytes per second in the future while maintaining data quality.
contributions: Single-kernel GPU compression design for efficiency
Lossless mode: 380.89-509.21 GB/s throughput (20x vs. industry leaders)
Configurable lossy modes with high compression ratios
Support for diverse integer dataset types
limitations: Abstract-only; specific light source facilities tested, absolute compression ratios, and scalability to future higher data rates not detailed.
primary_theme: Ultra-fast GPU compression for light source facilities
